71.why: [Adjudicated by hand after the two blind passes split (A said Quit India, B said Dandi). Champaran (1917) and the Second Round Table Conference (1931) are not occasions on which Gandhiji framed law-breaking as a duty, which leaves Dandi and Quit India. The Quit India launch has its own signature phrase, 'Do or Die', so a question setting a DIFFERENT quotation is unlikely to be pointing there; and declaring sedition a matter of religion fits the Civil Disobedience posture of open, deliberate, mass violation of a specific law, which is exactly what the Dandi salt-law breach was. Recorded honestly: this booklet carries no key, both passes rated this item their weakest in the packet, and the adjudication sides with the LOWER-confidence pass. It is the single item in this paper most worth checking against the official UPSC key if one is obtained.]
